messages.subject: divergent transitions when sampling
parts:
Hi,

For some reason I am receiving divergent transitions for this simple model:
parameters {
   real <lower=0> a;
   real <lower=0> b;
}
model {
   a ~ lognormal(0,1);
   b ~ lognormal(-0.6,0.35);
}

with fit <- stan(file='test.stan', warmup=0, iter=10, chains=1)

Can somebody explain why?

Thank you,
Linas

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: divergent transitions when sampling
parts:
Gabry,

Thanks a lot. Yes, I also get different # of divergent transitions every time I run the model. My question was really why divergent transitions even occur when I sample from two independent lognormals.

This example is just a simplified version of my model. I reality I estimate parameters of a large ODE model which runs for more then a day. Then my plan was to approximate posteriors with some standard distributions (I found that lognormal does a pretty good job) and sample from this approximated posterior so that in generated quantities I get the predictions I want (concentrations in blood plasma). I need to run several cycles of drug administration in order to get to steady state. I wanted to separate this exercise from parameter estimation since parameter estimation is so computationally expensive. The code is attached.

Linas

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: divergent transitions when sampling
parts:
Because you're using parameters/model instead of just the rng in generated quantities it is doing MCMC instead of just MC. That's ok, but because the inits are random here and because you basically have no warmup period you can still end up with some divergences because no auto-tuning of the sampler parameters has happened. I doubt you would see any post-warmup divergences if you gave it more warmup time. 

Jonah
